Archive item 1: Field Status Report – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Weekly)
Source format: Field Status Reports

| Equipment | Total Units | Status | Remarks |
|-----------|-------------|--------|---------|
| Camera traps (array) | 42 | Active | All deployed; routine maintenance ongoing |
| GPS units | 8 | Active | One unit (GPS-04) showing intermittent satellite lock; being monitored |
| Radio collars (tracking) | 6 | Active | All transmitting; battery levels healthy |
| Field vehicles | 2 | Maintenance | Gypsy (KA-18-M-4521) in workshop for clutch repair; Bolero operational |
| Weather station (Kerele) | 1 | Active | Rain gauge replaced on July 30 after bird damage |
| Solar power units (camera locations) | 12 | Active | Two units underperforming due to cloud cover; no action required |

The two vehicles are being managed with a revised rotation; the Bolero is prioritized for patrol duties, and the Gypsy is expected to return by August 6.

---

**3. Staffing and Attendance**

All field staff were present for the full week except for two personnel:

- **K. Manjunath (Field Assistant)** – On leave July 31 and August 1 (personal reasons).
- **P. Dinesh (Trainee)** – Attended a two-day GPS refresher workshop in Chikkamagaluru on August 1–2.

The anti-poaching camp at Hirekallu is fully staffed. One watcher (S. Gowda) reported for duty on August 3 after a one-day delay; he has been advised to inform the range office in advance for future travel delays. Temporary labor for trail clearing was hired for August 4–6, pending weather.

---

**4. Patrol and Monitoring Activities**

- **July 29:** Patrol of the eastern boundary (compartment 8–10). No signs of poaching or illegal logging. One snare was found and removed near the old salt lick site.
- **July 30:** Night patrol cancelled due to lightning. Day patrol observed a fresh tiger pugmark along the Kerele stream; photographs taken and logged.
- **July 31:** Heavy rain; patrol limited to vehicle-based route on the main road. Checked camera traps BT-12 and BT-14; both functioning.
- **August 1:** Foot patrol of compartment 15 (western range). Found one abandoned campfire site; no other evidence of intrusion.
- **August 2:** Short evening patrol (2 km) due to weather. Recorded elephant herd (approx. 8 individuals) near the waterhole at compartment 6.
- **August 3:** Redeployed cameras BT-17 and BT-29. Conducted a rapid assessment of the transect trail; cleared two small branches.
- **August 4:** Morning patrol of the southern boundary. No anomalies.

In the Field Status Report, the Bhadra Tiger Reserve camera trap array status is listed as active. Record status: current.

Patrol records are maintained in the daily log at the range office. Copies of the weekly summary have been shared with the Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) for review.

---

**5. Camera Trap Data and Observations**

Memory cards were collected from 10 camera units this week (BT-03, BT-06, BT-08, BT-11, BT-15, BT-18, BT-22, BT-25, BT-31, BT-33). Preliminary downloads were reviewed on August 4. Images include:

- Tiger (individual identified as T-7 based on stripe pattern) at BT-08 on July 30, 02:14 hrs.
- Leopard at BT-15 on July 29, 23:40 hrs.
- Dhole pack (4 individuals) at BT-22 on August 1, 06:05 hrs.
- Multiple sambar and wild pig captures across several units.

Data files have been backed up to the external drive and will be sent to the research cell for formal analysis. No camera unit showed signs of theft or tampering.

---

**6. Weather Summary**

| Date | Rainfall (mm) | Max Temp (°C) | Min Temp (°C) | Notes |
|------|---------------|----------------|----------------|-------|
| July 29 | 18 | 27 | 21 | Overcast |
| July 30 | 42 | 26 | 20 | Thunderstorm in evening |
| July 31 | 96 | 24 | 19 | Heavy rain; nullahs flooded |
| August 1 | 12 | 27 | 21 | Intermittent drizzle |
| August 2 | 38 | 26 | 20 | Rain in afternoon |
| August 3 | 5 | 28 | 22 | Partly cloudy |
| August 4 | 22 | 27 | 21 | Showers in morning |

The Kerele weather station recorded all readings; the rain gauge was replaced after the July 30 incident (bird damage) and has been accurate since.
**Field Status Report – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Weekly)**

**Report Period:** August 5 – 11, 2024
**Prepared by:** Field Coordinator, Bhadra Tiger Reserve
**Submitted to:** Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF), Bhadra Division
**Date of Submission:** August 12, 2024

---

**1. Patrol Summary**

Patrols were conducted daily across all major beats. The southern and eastern boundaries received priority due to the continued monsoon and reports of cattle grazing from adjacent villages.

- **August 5:** Full-day patrol of the eastern boundary (12 km). No signs of encroachment. One old snare (rusted, non-functional) recovered near compartment 14 and handed over to the range office.
- **August 6:** Patrol along the Kerele stream section. Water levels were high; crossing at the usual ford was not possible. Team took the longer route via the ridge line. No wildlife disturbance observed.
- **August 7:** Short patrol (4 km) in the morning due to heavy rain. Checked the area around the old fire watchtower; no issues. Afternoon spent on equipment maintenance at the base camp.
- **August 8:** Boundary patrol with the neighboring Kudremukh Wildlife Division team. Joint inspection of the shared boundary pillars. All pillars intact. Minor disagreement over the alignment of pillar 27; both sides noted the coordinates for further verification.
- **August 9:** Patrol of the core zone near compartment 8. Fresh pugmarks of a large male tiger recorded; plaster cast taken and stored at the range office. Likely the same individual photographed at BT-08 in the previous week.
- **August 10:** Morning patrol of the western boundary (6 km). No anomalies. In the afternoon, a team visited the site of the July 30 camera theft attempt; no further incidents reported.
- **August 11:** Day-long patrol covering the transect trail and the waterhole at compartment 6. The waterhole is full and attracting good numbers of prey species. Counted 14 sambar and a small herd of gaur (approx. 5 individuals) during a two-hour observation.

**Total patrol distance for the week:** 48 km (excluding joint patrol distance, which was logged separately).

---

**2. Staffing and Leave**

- **R. Kumar** (Field Assistant) was on casual leave on August 6 and 7. He returned to duty on August 8.
- **S. Patil** (Trainee) completed his one-month field attachment on August 9. His training log has been submitted to the ACF office. No extension has been requested.
- **M. Gowda** (Driver) is on weekly off on August 11. The vehicle will remain at the base camp.
- No other leave was recorded during the reporting period. All sanctioned posts are filled.

---

**3. Vehicle and Equipment Status**

- **Gypsy (KA-04-M-2387):** In service. The clutch issue noted in the previous report was attended to on August 6. A minor oil leak was detected on August 9; the vehicle is still in service but will be sent to the workshop after the coming week if the leak persists.
- **Motorcycle (KA-04-M-0912):** In service. Front tyre was replaced on August 8.
- **Camera traps:** The array status is **active**. All 35 units are deployed. Ten units were serviced this week (see Section 5).
- **GPS units:** All three units are functional. One unit (GPS-02) has a battery that drains faster than expected; spare batteries have been issued.
- **Rain gauge:** The replacement unit at the Kerele weather station is working accurately. No further issues.

---

**4. Camera Trap Data and Observations**

Memory cards were collected from 10 camera units this week: BT-02, BT-05, BT-09, BT-12, BT-17, BT-21, BT-24, BT-27, BT-29, and BT-34. Preliminary downloads were reviewed on August 11.

- **Tiger** (individual T-7, based on stripe pattern) photographed at BT-17 on August 7, 23:12 hrs. This is the same individual recorded at BT-08 on July 30, indicating movement across the northern section.
- **Leopard** at BT-02 on August 5, 04:55 hrs.
- **Dhole** (pack of 4) at BT-21 on August 9, 18:40 hrs.
- **Sloth bear** at BT-27 on August 10, 07:20 hrs. First sloth bear capture on this unit since March.
- Multiple captures of sambar, wild pig, and barking deer across several units.
- **BT-29** had no captures between August 3 and August 8. The unit was checked on August 9; the sensor was partially blocked by a fallen leaf. The leaf was removed, and the unit is functioning normally.

----- end of archived item -----

Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)
Field Logs

**Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)**
**Beat: Muthodi Range, Array Alpha transect**
**Log Keeper: A. Rao (Field Assistant) / R. Gowda (Trainee)**
**Period: 15 March 2024 – 20 March 2024**

---

**15 March 2024 (Friday)**

0600 hrs – Left base camp at Muthodi with R. Gowda and two local trackers (K. Manju, P. Suresh). Carried 12 camera trap units, 40 D-cell batteries, 4 memory cards (32 GB each), cable ties, straps, and 2 kg of rope. Weather clear, max temp later 34°C, no rain forecast for the week.

0730 hrs – Reached Array Alpha start point at the eastern boundary of compartment 12. Trail condition moderate; some elephant dung on the path, old (about 3 days). We cleared small branches blocking the trail at two points. No fresh pugmarks seen.

0915 hrs – Began camera placement. We are setting up a total of 12 units along a 2.4 km line, spaced roughly 200 m apart. Cameras set to motion-trigger, 3-shot burst, 1-minute delay, sensitivity high. All units tested with a quick hand-wave before mounting.

**Deployment note: The field log records the Camera Trap Array Alpha deployment date as 2024-03-15. Record status: historical.** All 12 cameras were mounted and armed by 1630 hrs. Units numbered CT-01 to CT-12. GPS coordinates recorded in the data sheet (attached). Batteries fresh, memory cards formatted on 14/3.

1730 hrs – Checked back at base. Entered initial data: camera ID, tree species, height (range 1.2–1.8 m), bearing (all facing north-east along the trail). No triggers yet (cameras armed only 1 hr before we left).

2100 hrs – Night patrol (2 km loop near the array). Heard sambar bark at 2130, no visuals. Dew point high, mist started around 2000 hrs.

---

**16 March 2024 (Saturday)**

0600 hrs – Morning inspection of Array Alpha. Walked the full 2.4 km line. All cameras present, no damage. One unit (CT-05) had a small ant nest on the strap; cleaned it off. Noted that CT-08's tree had a fresh scratch mark from a bear (probably sloth bear) – camera not knocked, but we re-secured the strap.

0930 hrs – Downloaded data from CT-01 to CT-04 (we carry a small laptop with card reader). Total triggers: 14 across 4 cameras. Mostly chital and wild pig. One clear photograph of a leopard at CT-03 at 0215 hrs (16/3) – first leopard for this array. Marked as "good capture" in the log.

1100 hrs – R. Gowda went back to base to charge batteries (we used 4 spare). I continued with trackers to check the western boundary of compartment 13 for any sign of cattle incursion. Found old cattle dung (dry) but no fresh tracks.

1400 hrs – Lunch break at the stream crossing. Water level low, about 20 cm deep. Noted some otter spraint on a rock near the crossing.

1600 hrs – Back at base. Updated the camera deployment register. All 12 units confirmed working. No theft or animal damage. Weather: hot, 35°C, no rain.

2100 hrs – Short night drive on the main road (10 km). Saw one mongoose, two hares. No large carnivores.

---

**17 March 2024 (Sunday)**

0645 hrs – Left base later than usual (R. Gowda had a minor stomach issue). Went straight to Array Alpha for a full download of all 12 cameras. Total triggers since deployment: 47 (all cameras). Breakdown by species (preliminary):
- Chital: 21
- Wild pig: 9
- Sambar: 6
- Leopard: 3 (CT-03, CT-07, CT-11)
- Jungle cat: 2
- Unidentified (too dark/blurred): 6

No tiger yet. The leopard at CT-07 was at 1830 hrs on 16/3 – evening activity. CT-11 had a leopard at 0505 hrs on 17/3 (morning).

1030 hrs – Replaced batteries in CT-05, CT-09, CT-12 (battery indicator showed low – these units may have been set to high sensitivity and triggered more). Replaced memory cards in all units (used 8 new cards, formatted earlier). Stored used cards in labeled bags.

1130 hrs – Trackers Manju and Suresh reported a fresh tiger pugmark near the stream crossing (about 300 m from CT-06). We went to verify. Pugmark size ~9 cm, clear, likely from the previous night (16/3). Direction: heading north-east, towards the core area. This is the first tiger sign in the array vicinity. We did not adjust camera positions, but noted the location in the log for future reference.
1015 hrs – Found a second scrape, smaller, on a tree base near a dry nullah. No hair this time. The nullah itself is dry, which is unusual for this time of year. We noted that the water sources in the northern part of compartment 14 are drying faster than last year.

1130 hrs – Rest break at the ridge. View of the valley is clear. No smoke seen in any direction – good for fire watch.

1230 hrs – Started the return leg, taking a different path through the bamboo patch. Manju spotted a crested serpent eagle on a nest. Noted the nest location (GPS: 13.712, 75.602) for the breeding bird survey next month.

1400 hrs – Back at base. Lunch. Washed the plaster cast and labeled it. Stored the hair sample in the fridge (the one we use for scat samples, left side, top shelf – please do not move it, it is next to the bait packets for the camera trap tests).

1530 hrs – Data entry: updated the pugmark register and the scrape log. The scrape at the termite mound is the second tiger sign in the array vicinity this season. The first was the pugmark on 16/3.

1700 hrs – Checked the weather station. Max temp today: 31°C. Humidity: 61%. Wind: moderate from the SW. No rain in the last 48 hrs.

---

**19 March 2024 (Tuesday)**

0600 hrs – Early start. R. Gowda and I went to Array Alpha to check CT-06 and CT-07, which are the units closest to the pugmark location. We wanted to see if any tiger had passed in front of them since the 16/3 sign.

0645 hrs – At CT-06. The unit had 8 triggers since 17/3 morning. Reviewing the images on the small screen:
- 4 triggers were chital (day and night)
- 2 were wild pig
- 1 was a jungle cat at 2210 hrs on 18/3
- 1 was a person on foot – that was us just now (we forgot to switch the camera to standby before approaching; our own trigger. Noted in the log as a self-trigger; will delete from the sequence.)

0740 hrs – At CT-07. 6 triggers. All chital and sambar. No tiger. The pugmark was about 300 m from CT-06, but the animal did not come into the camera cone. We discussed briefly whether to move CT-06 slightly to the west to cover the trail the tiger used, but decided to wait until we have more data. Moving cameras too often reduces our ability to compare seasonal patterns.

The field log notes that Dr. Anjali Rao actual survey date for Nagarahole was 2024-07-12. Record status: historical.

0900 hrs – Returned to base. Met the new volunteer, K. Pradeep, who arrived yesterday evening. He is a postgraduate student from Mangalore University, here for 8 weeks. Gave him the orientation talk: safety rules, what to do if he sees an elephant (back away slowly, do not run), how to use the GPS unit, and how to fill the daily log. He will mostly help with data entry and camera trap checks.

1030 hrs – Pradeep helped me clean the memory cards from the 17/3 download. We formatted 8 cards for the next deployment. He also labeled the bags for the used cards – good, he is careful.

1200 hrs – Lunch.

1400 hrs – Planned the work for the rest of the week. The main tasks are:
1. Full download of Array Bravo (12 cameras) – scheduled for 21/3
2. Check the salt lick and water hole camera (CT-13, a single unit near the eastern boundary) – 20/3
3. Fire watch patrol on the eastern boundary – 22/3
4. Prepare the monthly report for the DCF office – due 25/3

I noted that we are behind on the report because of the leopard captures and the extra time spent on the tiger sign. Will start drafting it on 23/3.

1700 hrs – Pradeep asked about the leopard photos. Showed him the CT-03 image from 16/3. He was impressed. Told him we do not share images outside the official reporting process until the DCF office clears them.

---

**20 March 2024 (Wednesday)**

0630 hrs – Left for the eastern boundary to check CT-13, the single camera near the salt lick and water hole. Pradeep came with me for his first field day. R. Gowda stayed at base to service the solar panels on the store room.

0745 hrs – At CT-13. The unit is mounted on a teak tree, about 4 m from the salt lick. The salt lick is heavily used – the ground is churned up with hoof prints. Fresh elephant dung about 30 m away (still steaming, so probably from early morning).
**Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)**
**Range: Muthodi Range | Beat: Kallur**
**Log Keeper: S. N. Hegde, Field Assistant**

---

**25 July 2024 (Thursday)**

0700 hrs – Started the day with the morning radio check. R. Gowda confirmed he will be at the
western boundary for the water hole camera repair. The spare housing unit from the DCF office
arrived yesterday evening, so he took that with him.

0745 hrs – Checked the rain gauge. Received 14 mm overnight. The stream near the K. Pradeep
transect is flowing well, which is good for the camera trap checks later this week.

0830 hrs – Received a message from the Range Forest Officer (RFO) office that the permit
extension for the ongoing carnivore sign survey has been approved. The extension covers the
period up to 15 August 2024. This is a relief – the earlier permit was due to expire on 31 July.
I will note the new validity in the monthly report.

0900 hrs – Left with Pradeep for the regular patrol along the northern boundary. The path near
the old teak plantation is overgrown. We noted that the boundary pillar No. 42 has fresh
elephant rub marks. The pillar is slightly tilted but still in position. We will report this
to the beat guard for corrective action.

1115 hrs – Reached the seasonal stream crossing. Found pug marks of a tigress with two cubs.
The prints are about a day old, heading east towards the core area. Pradeep took GPS
coordinates. We noted the location in the log: N 13°28' E 75°34', approximate elevation 850 m.

1300 hrs – Lunch break at the Pattighat check post. The guard there said he saw a leopard
crossing the road around 0600 hrs this morning. No livestock kills reported in the last week.

1430 hrs – Continued patrol. Checked the fire watch tower near the eastern boundary. The tower
is in good condition, but the water drum is empty. We refilled it from the stream. The fire
line clearing is still incomplete for about 2 km stretch. This needs to be done before the
dry season starts.

1600 hrs – Returned to base. Pradeep updated the camera trap deployment map on the wall.
He is getting better with the GPS unit. We discussed the plan for tomorrow – checking the
salt lick camera (CT-13) and downloading the memory cards from Array Alpha.

1700 hrs – Evening radio check. Gowda reported that the water hole camera (CT-08) is
working now after replacing the housing. He will be back by 1800 hrs.

---

**26 July 2024 (Friday)**

0630 hrs – Left for CT-13, the camera near the salt lick and water hole on the eastern
boundary. Pradeep came along. Gowda stayed at base to start the monthly report draft.

0745 hrs – At CT-13. The camera was triggered 12 times since the last check on 20/7.
The images show a herd of gaur (about 8 animals), a lone male elephant, and a leopard
passing at night. The camera battery is at 60%. No sign of damage to the housing.

0830 hrs – Checked the salt lick. It is heavily used. Fresh tiger pug marks were found
about 20 m from the camera, heading south. The prints are large – possibly the same male
tiger we photographed at CT-03 in March.

0930 hrs – Continued to the water hole. The water level is low but still sufficient.
Several bird species were seen, including the Malabar pied hornbill and the white-bellied
woodpecker.

1100 hrs – Started the memory card download for Array Alpha. We have 12 cameras in this
array. Pradeep helped with labeling the cards. The download went smoothly. We found
interesting captures including a leopard with cubs at CT-05, and a sloth bear at CT-09.
The bear sighting is noteworthy – we have not had a sloth bear at this array since
January.

1300 hrs – Lunch.

1400 hrs – Replaced the memory cards in the Array Alpha cameras. Pradeep formatted the
used cards. We will do the image review tomorrow.

1500 hrs – Started drafting the monthly report for the DCF office. The report is due on
31/7. I have the basic data ready – camera trap nights, species list, sign survey
results. I will add the permit extension details.

1600 hrs – Received a call from the RFO office about the leopard image from CT-03
(16/3). They want a higher resolution copy for their records. I will send it tomorrow
morning.
**Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)**

---

**28 July 2024 (Sunday)**

0630 hrs – Morning radio check with all three patrol teams. Weather clear, no rain overnight. The
stream near the western boundary is still flowing, but the level has dropped about 30 cm since the
monsoon peak.

0715 hrs – Left for the Array Alpha image review with Pradeep. Gowda went to the DCF office to
submit the monthly report draft and the permit extension application. He will call when he gets an
update.

0830 hrs – Started reviewing the images from the 12/7–26/7 download. Total 214 captures across
the 12 cameras. Of these, 89 are usable species records. The rest are blank triggers or vegetation
movement.

Key captures from the review:

- CT-01: Sambar (4 images, daytime)
- CT-03: Tiger, male, 16/3 image confirmed for RFO. High res copy sent to the RFO office at
  0930 hrs via the forest dept file transfer. Received confirmation of receipt at 1100 hrs.
- CT-05: Leopard with two cubs, 22/7, 2310 hrs. This is our first breeding evidence for leopard
  in Array Alpha since 2022. Noted in the monthly report as an important record.
- CT-09: Sloth bear, 25/7, 0545 hrs. Confirmed the earlier sighting. The monthly report now
  includes this as a notable species record for the array.

1100 hrs – Pradeep flagged that CT-06 had a bent mounting bracket. The camera was still
pointing in the right direction, but the bracket needs replacement. We do not have a spare in
the base store. I will request one from the Range Office.

1300 hrs – Lunch at base.

1400 hrs – Entered the species records into the database. We now have 27 species recorded in
Array Alpha for July. The species list for the monthly report is complete.

1500 hrs – Gowda called from the DCF office. The report was accepted. The permit extension
for the camera trap study (through 31/12/2024) is still pending – the DCF wants an additional
map of the camera locations. I will prepare the map tomorrow.

1600 hrs – Started preparing the map for the permit extension. I have the GPS coordinates for
all 36 cameras. I will mark the array boundaries and the main trails.

1700 hrs – Radio check. All teams reported back. No incidents.

---

**29 July 2024 (Monday)**

0630 hrs – Overcast, light drizzle. The ground is damp but workable.

0700 hrs – Continued the map for the permit extension. Pradeep helped with the GIS layer. The
map shows the three arrays (Alpha, Beta, Gamma), the camera positions, and the main patrol
trails.

0930 hrs – Gowda left for the DCF office with the map. He will submit it and wait for the
permit extension approval.

1000 hrs – Field day. Left for Array Beta to replace the CT-06 bracket. I had requested the
spare from the Range Office yesterday; they confirmed a bracket is available at the Muthodi
section. I will pick it up on the way.

1100 hrs – Picked up the bracket from Muthodi section. It is a standard housing bracket,
compatible with our cameras.

1130 hrs – At CT-06. Replaced the bracket. The camera is now securely mounted. The trigger
test worked fine. The camera was set to take 3 images per trigger, and the test produced 3
images as expected.

1230 hrs – While at CT-06, checked the nearby trail for sign. Found fresh elephant dung about
50 m from the camera. The dung was still warm, so the animal had passed recently. No crop
raiding reports from the nearby villages this week.

1300 hrs – Lunch.

1400 hrs – Continued to CT-04 to check the camera. The camera was triggered 8 times since
the last check. The images show a pack of dhole (4 animals) passing at dusk on 27/7. This is
our first dhole record for Array Beta this month.

1500 hrs – Returned to base. The drizzle had stopped by 1430 hrs.

1600 hrs – Gowda returned from the DCF office. The permit extension is approved – valid
through 31/12/2024. The signed copy is in the file. I have noted the approval in the monthly
report file.

1700 hrs – Radio check complete. All teams reported clear.

---

**30 July 2024 (Tuesday)**

0630 hrs – Clear morning, no rain. The stream near the western boundary has dropped further,
but the water hole at CT-13 still has sufficient water.

------------------------------------------------------------------

Deployment notes:
- Traps were set along animal trails, stream crossings, and ridge lines.
- Each trap was baited with scent lure (Caven's 2) for first 7 days, then removed.
- GPS coordinates recorded for each trap; see Annex A for full list.
- Two units (CTA-041, CTA-042) were not deployed; kept as spares at base.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. INITIAL CONFIGURATION PROTOCOL
------------------------------------------------------------------
All units were configured using the following standard settings before deployment:

Table 3.1 – Camera settings

| Parameter | Setting |
|-----------|---------|
| Image size | 3.1 MP (Reconyx), 20 MP (Bushnell) |
| Burst | 3 images per trigger |

Section 8 – Data Validation and Quality Control Logs

8.1 Overview

This section records quality control (QC) checks, error rates, and correction actions for the Camera Trap Array Alpha dataset for the period April–July 2024. The primary dataset under management is CAMTRAP-ALPHA-2024, comprising raw images, processed image files, and associated metadata (location, time, species identifications where applicable).

QC checks are performed at three stages:
1. Field-level checks: performed by field staff at the time of SD card download.
2. Ingestion-level checks: performed by the Data Manager (P. Menon) upon upload to the office server.
3. Analysis-level checks: performed by Research Assistant A. Rao prior to any analysis or model training.

All validation logs are maintained in the electronic logbook (filename: QC_LOG_ALPHA_2024.xlsx) and are backed up weekly as per the backup schedule in Section 7. Any discrepancies found during QC are recorded in Table 8.1a and are resolved within 5 working days unless otherwise noted.

8.2 Validation Checks Performed

The following validation checks are applied to each deployment cycle:

a) Image count check: The number of images recorded in the field log is compared with the actual number of files in the downloaded folder.
b) Timestamp check: The camera timestamp is compared with a reference time (GPS time) at the time of deployment and retrieval. A drift of more than 5 minutes is flagged.
c) File integrity check: A checksum (MD5) is computed for each image file. Files with mismatched checksums are flagged for re-download or re-copy.
d) Metadata check: The metadata embedded in each image (camera ID, location ID, date/time) is compared with the expected values from the deployment plan.
e) Blank frame check: Images with >90% black pixels are flagged as blank frames.
f) Species identification check: For images where species identification has been attempted, a random 10% sample is reviewed by a second observer.

Patrols were conducted daily across all major beats. The southern and eastern boundaries received priority due to the continued monsoon and reports of cattle grazing from adjacent villages.

- **August 5:** Full-day patrol of the eastern boundary (12 km). No signs of encroachment. One old snare (rusted, non-functional) recovered near compartment 14 and handed over to the range office.
- **August 6:** Patrol along the Kerele stream section. Water levels were high; crossing at the usual ford was not possible. Team took the longer route via the ridge line. No wildlife disturbance observed.
- **August 7:** Short patrol (4 km) in the morning due to heavy rain. Checked the area around the old fire watchtower; no issues. Afternoon spent on equipment maintenance at the base camp.
- **August 8:** Boundary patrol with the neighboring Kudremukh Wildlife Division team. Joint inspection of the shared boundary pillars. All pillars intact. Minor disagreement over the alignment of pillar 27; both sides noted the coordinates for further verification.
- **August 9:** Patrol of the core zone near compartment 8. Fresh pugmarks of a large male tiger recorded; plaster cast taken and stored at the range office. Likely the same individual photographed at BT-08 in the previous week.
- **August 10:** Morning patrol of the western boundary (6 km). No anomalies. In the afternoon, a team visited the site of the July 30 camera theft attempt; no further incidents reported.
- **August 11:** Day-long patrol covering the transect trail and the waterhole at compartment 6. The waterhole is full and attracting good numbers of prey species. Counted 14 sambar and a small herd of gaur (approx. 5 individuals) during a two-hour observation.

**Total patrol distance for the week:** 48 km (excluding joint patrol distance, which was logged separately).

---

**2. Staffing and Leave**

- **R. Kumar** (Field Assistant) was on casual leave on August 6 and 7. He returned to duty on August 8.
- **S. Patil** (Trainee) completed his one-month field attachment on August 9. His training log has been submitted to the ACF office. No extension has been requested.
- **M. Gowda** (Driver) is on weekly off on August 11. The vehicle will remain at the base camp.
- No other leave was recorded during the reporting period. All sanctioned posts are filled.

---

**3. Vehicle and Equipment Status**

- **Gypsy (KA-04-M-2387):** In service. The clutch issue noted in the previous report was attended to on August 6. A minor oil leak was detected on August 9; the vehicle is still in service but will be sent to the workshop after the coming week if the leak persists.
- **Motorcycle (KA-04-M-0912):** In service. Front tyre was replaced on August 8.
- **Camera traps:** The array status is **active**. All 35 units are deployed. Ten units were serviced this week (see Section 5).
- **GPS units:** All three units are functional. One unit (GPS-02) has a battery that drains faster than expected; spare batteries have been issued.
- **Rain gauge:** The replacement unit at the Kerele weather station is working accurately. No further issues.

---

**4. Camera Trap Data and Observations**

Memory cards were collected from 10 camera units this week: BT-02, BT-05, BT-09, BT-12, BT-17, BT-21, BT-24, BT-27, BT-29, and BT-34. Preliminary downloads were reviewed on August 11.

- **Tiger** (individual T-7, based on stripe pattern) photographed at BT-17 on August 7, 23:12 hrs. This is the same individual recorded at BT-08 on July 30, indicating movement across the northern section.
- **Leopard** at BT-02 on August 5, 04:55 hrs.
- **Dhole** (pack of 4) at BT-21 on August 9, 18:40 hrs.
- **Sloth bear** at BT-27 on August 10, 07:20 hrs. First sloth bear capture on this unit since March.
- Multiple captures of sambar, wild pig, and barking deer across several units.
- **BT-29** had no captures between August 3 and August 8. The unit was checked on August 9; the sensor was partially blocked by a fallen leaf. The leaf was removed, and the unit is functioning normally.

**Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)**
**Beat: Muthodi Range, Array Alpha transect**
**Log Keeper: A. Rao (Field Assistant) / R. Gowda (Trainee)**
**Period: 15 March 2024 – 20 March 2024**

---

**15 March 2024 (Friday)**

0600 hrs – Left base camp at Muthodi with R. Gowda and two local trackers (K. Manju, P. Suresh). Carried 12 camera trap units, 40 D-cell batteries, 4 memory cards (32 GB each), cable ties, straps, and 2 kg of rope. Weather clear, max temp later 34°C, no rain forecast for the week.

0730 hrs – Reached Array Alpha start point at the eastern boundary of compartment 12. Trail condition moderate; some elephant dung on the path, old (about 3 days). We cleared small branches blocking the trail at two points. No fresh pugmarks seen.

0915 hrs – Began camera placement. We are setting up a total of 12 units along a 2.4 km line, spaced roughly 200 m apart. Cameras set to motion-trigger, 3-shot burst, 1-minute delay, sensitivity high. All units tested with a quick hand-wave before mounting.

**Deployment note: The field log records the Camera Trap Array Alpha deployment date as 2024-03-15. Record status: historical.** All 12 cameras were mounted and armed by 1630 hrs. Units numbered CT-01 to CT-12. GPS coordinates recorded in the data sheet (attached). Batteries fresh, memory cards formatted on 14/3.

1730 hrs – Checked back at base. Entered initial data: camera ID, tree species, height (range 1.2–1.8 m), bearing (all facing north-east along the trail). No triggers yet (cameras armed only 1 hr before we left).

2100 hrs – Night patrol (2 km loop near the array). Heard sambar bark at 2130, no visuals. Dew point high, mist started around 2000 hrs.

---

**16 March 2024 (Saturday)**

0600 hrs – Morning inspection of Array Alpha. Walked the full 2.4 km line. All cameras present, no damage. One unit (CT-05) had a small ant nest on the strap; cleaned it off. Noted that CT-08's tree had a fresh scratch mark from a bear (probably sloth bear) – camera not knocked, but we re-secured the strap.

0930 hrs – Downloaded data from CT-01 to CT-04 (we carry a small laptop with card reader). Total triggers: 14 across 4 cameras. Mostly chital and wild pig. One clear photograph of a leopard at CT-03 at 0215 hrs (16/3) – first leopard for this array. Marked as "good capture" in the log.

1100 hrs – R. Gowda went back to base to charge batteries (we used 4 spare). I continued with trackers to check the western boundary of compartment 13 for any sign of cattle incursion. Found old cattle dung (dry) but no fresh tracks.

1400 hrs – Lunch break at the stream crossing. Water level low, about 20 cm deep. Noted some otter spraint on a rock near the crossing.

1600 hrs – Back at base. Updated the camera deployment register. All 12 units confirmed working. No theft or animal damage. Weather: hot, 35°C, no rain.

2100 hrs – Short night drive on the main road (10 km). Saw one mongoose, two hares. No large carnivores.

---

**17 March 2024 (Sunday)**

0645 hrs – Left base later than usual (R. Gowda had a minor stomach issue). Went straight to Array Alpha for a full download of all 12 cameras. Total triggers since deployment: 47 (all cameras). Breakdown by species (preliminary):
- Chital: 21
- Wild pig: 9
- Sambar: 6
- Leopard: 3 (CT-03, CT-07, CT-11)
- Jungle cat: 2
- Unidentified (too dark/blurred): 6

No tiger yet. The leopard at CT-07 was at 1830 hrs on 16/3 – evening activity. CT-11 had a leopard at 0505 hrs on 17/3 (morning).

1030 hrs – Replaced batteries in CT-05, CT-09, CT-12 (battery indicator showed low – these units may have been set to high sensitivity and triggered more). Replaced memory cards in all units (used 8 new cards, formatted earlier). Stored used cards in labeled bags.

1130 hrs – Trackers Manju and Suresh reported a fresh tiger pugmark near the stream crossing (about 300 m from CT-06). We went to verify. Pugmark size ~9 cm, clear, likely from the previous night (16/3). Direction: heading north-east, towards the core area. This is the first tiger sign in the array vicinity. We did not adjust camera positions, but noted the location in the log for future reference.

documents.title: Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)
documents.content:
1015 hrs – Found a second scrape, smaller, on a tree base near a dry nullah. No hair this time. The nullah itself is dry, which is unusual for this time of year. We noted that the water sources in the northern part of compartment 14 are drying faster than last year.

1130 hrs – Rest break at the ridge. View of the valley is clear. No smoke seen in any direction – good for fire watch.

1230 hrs – Started the return leg, taking a different path through the bamboo patch. Manju spotted a crested serpent eagle on a nest. Noted the nest location (GPS: 13.712, 75.602) for the breeding bird survey next month.

1400 hrs – Back at base. Lunch. Washed the plaster cast and labeled it. Stored the hair sample in the fridge (the one we use for scat samples, left side, top shelf – please do not move it, it is next to the bait packets for the camera trap tests).

1530 hrs – Data entry: updated the pugmark register and the scrape log. The scrape at the termite mound is the second tiger sign in the array vicinity this season. The first was the pugmark on 16/3.

1700 hrs – Checked the weather station. Max temp today: 31°C. Humidity: 61%. Wind: moderate from the SW. No rain in the last 48 hrs.

---

**19 March 2024 (Tuesday)**

0600 hrs – Early start. R. Gowda and I went to Array Alpha to check CT-06 and CT-07, which are the units closest to the pugmark location. We wanted to see if any tiger had passed in front of them since the 16/3 sign.

0645 hrs – At CT-06. The unit had 8 triggers since 17/3 morning. Reviewing the images on the small screen:
- 4 triggers were chital (day and night)
- 2 were wild pig
- 1 was a jungle cat at 2210 hrs on 18/3
- 1 was a person on foot – that was us just now (we forgot to switch the camera to standby before approaching; our own trigger. Noted in the log as a self-trigger; will delete from the sequence.)

0740 hrs – At CT-07. 6 triggers. All chital and sambar. No tiger. The pugmark was about 300 m from CT-06, but the animal did not come into the camera cone. We discussed briefly whether to move CT-06 slightly to the west to cover the trail the tiger used, but decided to wait until we have more data. Moving cameras too often reduces our ability to compare seasonal patterns.

The field log notes that Dr. Anjali Rao actual survey date for Nagarahole was 2024-07-12. Record status: historical.

0900 hrs – Returned to base. Met the new volunteer, K. Pradeep, who arrived yesterday evening. He is a postgraduate student from Mangalore University, here for 8 weeks. Gave him the orientation talk: safety rules, what to do if he sees an elephant (back away slowly, do not run), how to use the GPS unit, and how to fill the daily log. He will mostly help with data entry and camera trap checks.

1030 hrs – Pradeep helped me clean the memory cards from the 17/3 download. We formatted 8 cards for the next deployment. He also labeled the bags for the used cards – good, he is careful.

1200 hrs – Lunch.

1400 hrs – Planned the work for the rest of the week. The main tasks are:
1. Full download of Array Bravo (12 cameras) – scheduled for 21/3
2. Check the salt lick and water hole camera (CT-13, a single unit near the eastern boundary) – 20/3
3. Fire watch patrol on the eastern boundary – 22/3
4. Prepare the monthly report for the DCF office – due 25/3

I noted that we are behind on the report because of the leopard captures and the extra time spent on the tiger sign. Will start drafting it on 23/3.

1700 hrs – Pradeep asked about the leopard photos. Showed him the CT-03 image from 16/3. He was impressed. Told him we do not share images outside the official reporting process until the DCF office clears them.

---

**20 March 2024 (Wednesday)**

0630 hrs – Left for the eastern boundary to check CT-13, the single camera near the salt lick and water hole. Pradeep came with me for his first field day. R. Gowda stayed at base to service the solar panels on the store room.

0745 hrs – At CT-13. The unit is mounted on a teak tree, about 4 m from the salt lick. The salt lick is heavily used – the ground is churned up with hoof prints. Fresh elephant dung about 30 m away (still steaming, so probably from early morning).

documents.content:
**Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)**
**Range: Muthodi Range | Beat: Kallur**
**Log Keeper: S. N. Hegde, Field Assistant**

---

**25 July 2024 (Thursday)**

0700 hrs – Started the day with the morning radio check. R. Gowda confirmed he will be at the
western boundary for the water hole camera repair. The spare housing unit from the DCF office
arrived yesterday evening, so he took that with him.

0745 hrs – Checked the rain gauge. Received 14 mm overnight. The stream near the K. Pradeep
transect is flowing well, which is good for the camera trap checks later this week.

0830 hrs – Received a message from the Range Forest Officer (RFO) office that the permit
extension for the ongoing carnivore sign survey has been approved. The extension covers the
period up to 15 August 2024. This is a relief – the earlier permit was due to expire on 31 July.
I will note the new validity in the monthly report.

0900 hrs – Left with Pradeep for the regular patrol along the northern boundary. The path near
the old teak plantation is overgrown. We noted that the boundary pillar No. 42 has fresh
elephant rub marks. The pillar is slightly tilted but still in position. We will report this
to the beat guard for corrective action.

1115 hrs – Reached the seasonal stream crossing. Found pug marks of a tigress with two cubs.
The prints are about a day old, heading east towards the core area. Pradeep took GPS
coordinates. We noted the location in the log: N 13°28' E 75°34', approximate elevation 850 m.

1300 hrs – Lunch break at the Pattighat check post. The guard there said he saw a leopard
crossing the road around 0600 hrs this morning. No livestock kills reported in the last week.

1430 hrs – Continued patrol. Checked the fire watch tower near the eastern boundary. The tower
is in good condition, but the water drum is empty. We refilled it from the stream. The fire
line clearing is still incomplete for about 2 km stretch. This needs to be done before the
dry season starts.

1600 hrs – Returned to base. Pradeep updated the camera trap deployment map on the wall.
He is getting better with the GPS unit. We discussed the plan for tomorrow – checking the
salt lick camera (CT-13) and downloading the memory cards from Array Alpha.

1700 hrs – Evening radio check. Gowda reported that the water hole camera (CT-08) is
working now after replacing the housing. He will be back by 1800 hrs.

---

**26 July 2024 (Friday)**

0630 hrs – Left for CT-13, the camera near the salt lick and water hole on the eastern
boundary. Pradeep came along. Gowda stayed at base to start the monthly report draft.

0745 hrs – At CT-13. The camera was triggered 12 times since the last check on 20/7.
The images show a herd of gaur (about 8 animals), a lone male elephant, and a leopard
passing at night. The camera battery is at 60%. No sign of damage to the housing.

0830 hrs – Checked the salt lick. It is heavily used. Fresh tiger pug marks were found
about 20 m from the camera, heading south. The prints are large – possibly the same male
tiger we photographed at CT-03 in March.

0930 hrs – Continued to the water hole. The water level is low but still sufficient.
Several bird species were seen, including the Malabar pied hornbill and the white-bellied
woodpecker.

1100 hrs – Started the memory card download for Array Alpha. We have 12 cameras in this
array. Pradeep helped with labeling the cards. The download went smoothly. We found
interesting captures including a leopard with cubs at CT-05, and a sloth bear at CT-09.
The bear sighting is noteworthy – we have not had a sloth bear at this array since
January.

1300 hrs – Lunch.

1400 hrs – Replaced the memory cards in the Array Alpha cameras. Pradeep formatted the
used cards. We will do the image review tomorrow.

1500 hrs – Started drafting the monthly report for the DCF office. The report is due on
31/7. I have the basic data ready – camera trap nights, species list, sign survey
results. I will add the permit extension details.

1600 hrs – Received a call from the RFO office about the leopard image from CT-03
(16/3). They want a higher resolution copy for their records. I will send it tomorrow
morning.

documents.content:
**Field Log – Bhadra Tiger Reserve (Daily)**

---

**28 July 2024 (Sunday)**

0630 hrs – Morning radio check with all three patrol teams. Weather clear, no rain overnight. The
stream near the western boundary is still flowing, but the level has dropped about 30 cm since the
monsoon peak.

0715 hrs – Left for the Array Alpha image review with Pradeep. Gowda went to the DCF office to
submit the monthly report draft and the permit extension application. He will call when he gets an
update.

0830 hrs – Started reviewing the images from the 12/7–26/7 download. Total 214 captures across
the 12 cameras. Of these, 89 are usable species records. The rest are blank triggers or vegetation
movement.

Key captures from the review:

- CT-01: Sambar (4 images, daytime)
- CT-03: Tiger, male, 16/3 image confirmed for RFO. High res copy sent to the RFO office at
  0930 hrs via the forest dept file transfer. Received confirmation of receipt at 1100 hrs.
- CT-05: Leopard with two cubs, 22/7, 2310 hrs. This is our first breeding evidence for leopard
  in Array Alpha since 2022. Noted in the monthly report as an important record.
- CT-09: Sloth bear, 25/7, 0545 hrs. Confirmed the earlier sighting. The monthly report now
  includes this as a notable species record for the array.

1100 hrs – Pradeep flagged that CT-06 had a bent mounting bracket. The camera was still
pointing in the right direction, but the bracket needs replacement. We do not have a spare in
the base store. I will request one from the Range Office.

1300 hrs – Lunch at base.

1400 hrs – Entered the species records into the database. We now have 27 species recorded in
Array Alpha for July. The species list for the monthly report is complete.

1500 hrs – Gowda called from the DCF office. The report was accepted. The permit extension
for the camera trap study (through 31/12/2024) is still pending – the DCF wants an additional
map of the camera locations. I will prepare the map tomorrow.

1600 hrs – Started preparing the map for the permit extension. I have the GPS coordinates for
all 36 cameras. I will mark the array boundaries and the main trails.

1700 hrs – Radio check. All teams reported back. No incidents.

---

**29 July 2024 (Monday)**

0630 hrs – Overcast, light drizzle. The ground is damp but workable.

0700 hrs – Continued the map for the permit extension. Pradeep helped with the GIS layer. The
map shows the three arrays (Alpha, Beta, Gamma), the camera positions, and the main patrol
trails.

0930 hrs – Gowda left for the DCF office with the map. He will submit it and wait for the
permit extension approval.

1000 hrs – Field day. Left for Array Beta to replace the CT-06 bracket. I had requested the
spare from the Range Office yesterday; they confirmed a bracket is available at the Muthodi
section. I will pick it up on the way.

1100 hrs – Picked up the bracket from Muthodi section. It is a standard housing bracket,
compatible with our cameras.

1130 hrs – At CT-06. Replaced the bracket. The camera is now securely mounted. The trigger
test worked fine. The camera was set to take 3 images per trigger, and the test produced 3
images as expected.

1230 hrs – While at CT-06, checked the nearby trail for sign. Found fresh elephant dung about
50 m from the camera. The dung was still warm, so the animal had passed recently. No crop
raiding reports from the nearby villages this week.

1300 hrs – Lunch.

1400 hrs – Continued to CT-04 to check the camera. The camera was triggered 8 times since
the last check. The images show a pack of dhole (4 animals) passing at dusk on 27/7. This is
our first dhole record for Array Beta this month.

1500 hrs – Returned to base. The drizzle had stopped by 1430 hrs.

1600 hrs – Gowda returned from the DCF office. The permit extension is approved – valid
through 31/12/2024. The signed copy is in the file. I have noted the approval in the monthly
report file.

1700 hrs – Radio check complete. All teams reported clear.

---

**30 July 2024 (Tuesday)**

0630 hrs – Clear morning, no rain. The stream near the western boundary has dropped further,
but the water hole at CT-13 still has sufficient water.

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. ARRAY CONFIGURATION SUMMARY (CURRENT)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Table 1.1 – Trap unit inventory (current controlled entry)

The inventory record shows the Camera Trap Array Alpha number of trap units as 42. Record status: current. This count includes all deployed and spare units as of the current inventory. No units have been removed from the array since initial deployment; two units are held as spares at the base station.

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. DEPLOYMENT LOG – MARCH 2024
------------------------------------------------------------------
Deployment window: 05–14 Mar 2024 (10 days)
Field team: A. Rao (lead), P. Kulkarni, M. Fernandes, J. D'Souza, local guide (G. Gowda)

| T4 – Buffer | 6 | N 12.5978, E 75.8100 | 380–520 | Degraded forest, plantation edge |

Total units deployed: 42 (12 + 14 + 10 + 6 = 42)

Deployment notes:
- Traps were set along animal trails, stream crossings, and ridge lines.
- Each trap was baited with scent lure (Caven's 2) for first 7 days, then removed.
- GPS coordinates recorded for each trap; see Annex A for full list.
- Two units (CTA-041, CTA-042) were not deployed; kept as spares at base.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. INITIAL CONFIGURATION PROTOCOL
------------------------------------------------------------------
All units were configured using the following standard settings before deployment:

Table 3.1 – Camera settings

| Parameter | Setting |
|-----------|---------|
| Image size | 3.1 MP (Reconyx), 20 MP (Bushnell) |
| Burst | 3 images per trigger |
| Trigger interval | 1 sec (Reconyx), 2 sec (Bushnell) |
| Sensitivity | High |
| Night mode | Infrared (IR) |
| Time stamp | On (24-hr format) |
| Camera name | CTA-XXX (e.g., CTA-001) |
| Password | Set per unit (see Annex B) |
| Date/time | Synchronized with GPS at deployment |

Firmware:
- Reconyx units: updated to v6.3.2 on 04 Mar 2024 (all 36 units)
- Bushnell units: firmware v1.2.3 (all 6 units, no update available)

SD card preparation:
- All cards formatted to FAT32 using the provided formatter.
- Card label written on the card itself (e.g., "CTA-001 T1").
- Each card was tested with a quick capture before deployment.

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. DATA COLLECTION PROTOCOLS (STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE)
------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 Image capture
- Cameras operate continuously, 24 hours a day.
- Images are stored on the SD card in the camera.
- Each trigger event produces a burst of 3 images (1 sec interval).

4.2 Retrieval schedule
- Traps are checked every 21 days (3-week cycle).
- Cycle 1: 25 Mar–04 Apr 2024
- Cycle 2: 15–25 Apr 2024
- Cycle 3: 06–16 May 2024
- Cycle 4: 27 May–06 Jun 2024
- Cycle 5: 17–27 Jun 2024
- Cycle 6: 08–18 Jul 2024
- Cycle 7: 29 Jul–08 Aug 2024
- Cycle 8: 19–29 Aug 2024

4.3 Data download and backup
- At each check, SD cards are swapped with fresh cards.
- Downloaded images are transferred to the field laptop (Dell Latitude 5420).
- Backup is created on two external HDDs (WD 2TB, Seagate 2TB) – one kept at base, one at field station.
- Backup log is maintained (see Section 5).

Section 8 – Data Validation and Quality Control Logs

8.1 Overview

This section records quality control (QC) checks, error rates, and correction actions for the Camera Trap Array Alpha dataset for the period April–July 2024. The primary dataset under management is CAMTRAP-ALPHA-2024, comprising raw images, processed image files, and associated metadata (location, time, species identifications where applicable).

QC checks are performed at three stages:
1. Field-level checks: performed by field staff at the time of SD card download.
2. Ingestion-level checks: performed by the Data Manager (P. Menon) upon upload to the office server.
3. Analysis-level checks: performed by Research Assistant A. Rao prior to any analysis or model training.

All validation logs are maintained in the electronic logbook (filename: QC_LOG_ALPHA_2024.xlsx) and are backed up weekly as per the backup schedule in Section 7. Any discrepancies found during QC are recorded in Table 8.1a and are resolved within 5 working days unless otherwise noted.

8.2 Validation Checks Performed

The following validation checks are applied to each deployment cycle:

a) Image count check: The number of images recorded in the field log is compared with the actual number of files in the downloaded folder.
b) Timestamp check: The camera timestamp is compared with a reference time (GPS time) at the time of deployment and retrieval. A drift of more than 5 minutes is flagged.
c) File integrity check: A checksum (MD5) is computed for each image file. Files with mismatched checksums are flagged for re-download or re-copy.
d) Metadata check: The metadata embedded in each image (camera ID, location ID, date/time) is compared with the expected values from the deployment plan.
e) Blank frame check: Images with >90% black pixels are flagged as blank frames.
f) Species identification check: For images where species identification has been attempted, a random 10% sample is reviewed by a second observer.
